# Statistical Analysis for Distal-Proximal Gradient

## Hierarchical Model Building Strategy

### Model m0: Baseline (Random Intercept Only)

This baseline model quantifies between-participant variability without any predictors.

```{r dpg-m0}
m0_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 1 + (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m0_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m0 <- confint(m0_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m0)
```

### Model m1a: Add Light Lag 0 (Current Day)

This model adds the current day light exposure variable as a fixed effect with Light_Lag0_num.

```{r dpg-m1a}
m1a_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1a_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1a <- confint(m1a_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1a)
```

### Model m1b: Add Light Lag 1 Additionally (One Day Before)

This model adds the light exposure one day before as a fixed effect using Light_Lag1_num.

```{r dpg-m1b}
m1b_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1b_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1b <- confint(m1b_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1b)
```

### Model m1c: Add Light Lag 2 Additionally (Two Days Before)

This model adds the light exposure two days before as a fixed effect with Light_Lag2_num.

```{r dpg-m1c}
m1c_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1c_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c <- confint(m1c_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c)
```

### Likelihood Ratio Tests: Lag Effects

```{r likelihood-ratio-tests-lag-effects}
# LRT 1: Does adding Lag 0 improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m0_vs_m1a_dpg <- anova(m0_dpg, m1a_dpg)

# LRT 2: Does adding Lag 1 improve fit over Lag 0 only?
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_dpg <- anova(m1a_dpg, m1b_dpg)

# LRT 3: Does adding Lag 2 improve fit over Lag 0 + Lag 1?
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_dpg <- anova(m1b_dpg, m1c_dpg)

# Display results
lrt_m0_vs_m1a_dpg
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_dpg
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_dpg
```

Interpretation Likelihood Ratio Tests Lag Effects:

-   LRT 1: Adding Lag 0 did not improve fit over the baseline model only (m0 vs. m1a: χ²=1.0387, p=0.3081)

-   LRT 2: Adding Lag 1 did not significantly improve fit over model m1a_dpg (m1a vs. m1b: χ²=0.2919, p=0.589)

-   LRT 3: Adding Lag 2 did not significantly improve fit over model m1b_dpg (m1b vs. m1c: χ²=0.0754, p=0.7836)

### Model m2: Add Linear Session Effect

This model adds a linear session term to account for potential temporal trends across the study.

```{r model-m2}
m2_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 
    exp_session +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m2_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2 <- confint(m2_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2)
```

### Model m3: Add Quadratic Session Effekct

This model tests for non-linear temporal trends (e.g., U-shaped patterns) across sessions.

```{r model-m3}
m3_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 
    exp_session + I(exp_session^2) +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m3_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m3 <- confint(m3_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m3)
```

### Likelihood Ratio Tests: Session Effects

```{r likelihood-ratio-tests-session-effects}
# LRT 1: Does adding exp_session (linear) improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m0_vs_m2_dpg <- anova(m0_dpg, m2_dpg)

# LRT 2: Does adding quadratic term improve fit over linear only?
lrt_m2_vs_m3_dpg <- anova(m2_dpg, m3_dpg)

lrt_m0_vs_m2_dpg
lrt_m2_vs_m3_dpg
```

Interpretation Likelihood Ratio Tests Session Effects: - Adding a linear session term did not improve model fit over the baseline only model (m0 vs. m2: χ²=2.3853, p=0.1225)

-   Adding a quadratic session term did not improve model fit over model m2 (m2 vs. m3: χ²=0.8772, p=0.349)

## Model Selection Summary

Based on LRT test results, model m0_dpg with the random intercept only was chosen as the final model. All other models did not find significant light or session effects of DPG values in this group.

-   Model m1a_dpg: Lag 0 (β=0.2325, SE=0.2271, p=0.31); AIC=199.0, BIC=207.7

-   Model m1b_dpg: Lag 0 (β=0.2274, SE=0.2268, p=0.320); Lag 1 (β=-0.1222, SE=0.2260, p=0.591); AIC=200.7, BIC=211.6

-   Model m1c_dpg: Lag 0 (β=0.22274, SE=0.22726, p=0.331); Lag 1 (β=-0.11959, SE=0.22602, p=0.599); Lag 2 (β=-0.06224, SE=0.22651, p=0.784); AIC=202.6, BIC=215.7

-   Model m2_dpg: Linear Session Term (β=-0.06925, SE=0.04425, p=0.123); AIC=197.6, BIC=206.3

-   Model m3_dpg: Quadratic Session Term (β=0.01634, SE=0.01739, p=0.351012); AIC=198.8, BIC=209.6

## Diagnostics Summary

### Check 1: Normality Assumption for Residuals

```{r normality-residuals}
# Q-Q Plot Residuals
qqnorm(resid(m0_dpg), main = "Q-Q Plot: Residuals")
qqline(resid(m0_dpg), col = "red")

# Shapiro-Wilk Test 
shapiro.test(resid(m0_dpg))
```

Interpretation Check 1 Normality Assumption for Residuals: Normality assumption for residuals seems to be adequately met. Both visual inspection of the QQ-plot shows good alignment with the theoretical normal distribution with minor deviations in the lower and upper tails, likely attributable to the relatively small sample size. Also the Shapiro-Wilk Test did not find evidence against the normality of residuals (W=0.98497, p=0.6175).

### Check 2: Distribution of Residuals

```{r distribution-residuals}
# Histogram with Density Curve
ggplot(data.frame(residuals = resid(m0_dpg)), aes(x = residuals)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 20, 
                 fill = "#4A90E2", alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  geom_density(color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Residuals (m0_dpg)",
       x = "Residuals", y = "Density") +
  theme_classic()
```

Interpretation Check 2 Distribution of Residuals: Consistent with the Q-Q plot findings, the histogram shows approximately normally distributed residuals with no extreme outliers.

### Check 3: Normality of Random Effects

```{r normality-random-effects}
# Q-Q Plot of Random Effects (Intercepts)
qqnorm(ranef(m0_dpg)$participant_id[,1], 
       main = "Q-Q Plot: Random Intercepts")
qqline(ranef(m0_dpg)$participant_id[,1], col = "red")
```

Interpretation Check 3 Normality of Random Effects: Acknowledging the limited interpretability due to the small number of random intercepts (n = 8), the assumption of normally distributed random effects appears to be reasonably met.

### Check 4: Variance Components and ICC

```{r variance-compoenents-icc}
# Intraclass Correlation Coefficient
icc(m0_dpg)

# Model Performance
model_performance(m0_dpg)
```

Interpretation Check 4 ICC: Approximately 54% of the total variance in DPG values is attributeable to between-participant differences, while the remaining 46% reflect the within-participant differences.

### Check 5: Heteroscedasticity

```{r heteroscedasticity}
# Check for heteroscedasticity across participants
df_resid <- data.frame(
  participant_id = ibuttons_lmm$participant_id,
  residuals = resid(m0_dpg)
)

ggplot(df_resid, aes(x = participant_id, y = residuals)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#4A90E2", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Residuals by Participant (m0_dpg)",
       x = "Participant", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Interpretation Check 5 Heteroscedasticity: Residual variances appeared reasonably consistent across participants, supporting model assumptions.

### Check 6: Temporal Patterns

```{r temporal-patterns}
# Check for temporal patterns
df_resid_time <- data.frame(
  exp_session = ibuttons_lmm$exp_session,
  residuals = resid(m0_dpg)
)

ggplot(df_resid_time, aes(x = exp_session, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residuals across Sessions (m0_dpg)",
       x = "Experimental Session", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_classic()
```

Interpretation Check 6 Temporal Patterns: From Session 3 to around Session 8 a systematic downward trend is visible with a plateau at the end. Whereas session 11-13 are not well suited for interpretation due to the sparse data (n=3 for session 11, 12 and n=1 for session 13). The LOESS smooth confirms this pattern, suggesting a potential session effect not captured by the baseline model. This temporal pattern indicates that DPG may systematically decrease across experimental sessions, which was not detected as statistically significant in likelihood ratio tests (m0 vs m2: p=0.12), possibly due to limited statistical power (n=8 participants).

# Sensitivity Analysis

## Sensitivity Analysis 1: Exclude P06 (Problematic Outliers)

Rationale: P06 showed extensive outliers during data cleaning (30-50%), potentially biasing model estimates. This sensitivity analysis tests model robustness by excluding P06 (n=7 participants remaining).

```{r sensitivity-exclude-p06-data}
# Create subset without P06
ibuttons_lmm_sens <- ibuttons_lmm %>%
  filter(participant_id != "P06")

# Summary
cat("Original dataset: n =", nrow(ibuttons_lmm), "observations,", 
    length(unique(ibuttons_lmm$participant_id)), "participants\n")
cat("Sensitivity dataset: n =", nrow(ibuttons_lmm_sens), "observations,", 
    length(unique(ibuttons_lmm_sens$participant_id)), "participants\n")
```

```{r sensitivity-exclude-p06-summary}
# Descriptive statistics comparison
data.frame(
  Dataset = c("Original (n=8)", "Sensitivity (n=7, P06 excluded)"),
  N_obs = c(nrow(ibuttons_lmm), nrow(ibuttons_lmm_sens)),
  Mean = c(mean(ibuttons_lmm$DPG_intervention), 
           mean(ibuttons_lmm_sens$DPG_intervention)),
  SD = c(sd(ibuttons_lmm$DPG_intervention), 
         sd(ibuttons_lmm_sens$DPG_intervention)),
  Min = c(min(ibuttons_lmm$DPG_intervention), 
          min(ibuttons_lmm_sens$DPG_intervention)),
  Max = c(max(ibuttons_lmm$DPG_intervention), 
          max(ibuttons_lmm_sens$DPG_intervention))
) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, 
        caption = "Descriptive statistics: Original vs. Sensitivity Analysis (P06 excluded)")
```

Interpretation Sensitivity 1 (Excluding P06 out of the analysis due to a lot of outliers identified): Conclusions drawn from the analysis and hierarchiechal model building using the entire dataset were not changed comapred to using the dataset, which excludes P06 from the analysis.

# Exploratory Analyses

## Exploratory Analysis 1: Random Slopes for Light_Lag0

Rationale: The primary models (m1a-m1c) assumed that light effects are identical across all participants (fixed slopes). This exploratory analysis tests whether participants vary in their response to current-day light exposure by fitting random slopes for Light_Lag0.

```{r dpg-random-slope-lag0}
# Fit model with random slopes for Light_Lag0
m1c_dpg_rs_lag0 <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 + Light_Lag0_num | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm, 
  REML = FALSE, 
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

summary(m1c_dpg_rs_lag0)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c_dpg_rs_lag0 <- confint(m1c_dpg_rs_lag0, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c_dpg_rs_lag0)
```

Interpretation Exploratory Analysis 1 Random Slopes for Light_Lag0: The model with random slopes for Light_Lag0 resulted in a singular fit (correlation between random intercept and slope = 1.00), indicating that the data do not support individual variation in current-day light exposure effects. The random slope variance was minimal (SD = 0.18) and fully confounded with the random intercept structure.

## Exploratory Analysis 2: Age and Sex Moderation

Rationale: To test whether the skin temperature gradient is influenced by biological sex or age.

```{r age-sex-moderation}
# Fit model with age and sex 
# Center age
ibuttons_lmm <- ibuttons_lmm %>%
  mutate(age_c = age - mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))

# Moderation model 
dpg_moderation <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 
    sex + age_c +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(dpg_moderation)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_dpg_moderation <- confint(dpg_moderation, method = "Wald")
print(ci_dpg_moderation)
```

Interpretation Exploratory Analysis 2 Age and Sex Moderation: No statistically significant main effect was found of biological sex (male with female as reference category: β=0.35296, SE=0.84021, p=0.686) or age (centered: β=-0.02889, SE=0.10711, p=0.794). As no statistically signficant effects of the different light exposure variables or the experimental session number were found, no interactions between demographic factors and such fixed effects could be investigated.

## Exploratory Analysis 3: Light Lag Interactions

Rationale: Despite finding no significant main effects of light exposure on the current day or one or two days prior, all two-way interactions between the different Light Lags will be tested.

```{r lag-interactions}
dpg_interactions <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num * Light_Lag1_num + 
    Light_Lag0_num * Light_Lag2_num +
    Light_Lag1_num * Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(dpg_interactions)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_dpg_interactions <- confint(dpg_interactions, method = "Wald")
print(ci_dpg_interactions)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 3 Light Lag Interactions: When including the interaction terms between the different Light Lags, the following results emerged:

-   Light Lag 2: significant effect of Lag 2 for the DPG with bright light two days prior suggesting, that bright light exposure two days prior is associated with a more negative DPG of around -0.8°C (β=-0.797319, SE=0.379887, p=0.0403) when controlling for interactions.

-   Light Lag 0 x Light Lag 2 Interaction: A significant positive interaction term between Lag 0 and Lag 2 was found (β=1.118357, SE=0.429289, p=0.0117). This interaction indicates that the effect of Lag2 depends on current-day light exposure: when both Lag0 and Lag2 are bright, the combined effect is less negative than would be predicted by adding the individual effects (non-additive relationship).

All other effects and interactions were not statistically significant (p\>0.3). Despite the exploratory nature of this Light Lag Interactions model, a rather synergistic effect of current evenings light exposure with the light exposure 2 days prior on current evenings DPG values can be found, whereby current bright light appears to attenuate the effect of bright light from two days ago.

## Exploratory Analysis 4: Persistence Analysis

Rationale: The persistence analysis for DPG addresses the question: Does the number of consecutive days of the same light condition (run length) modulate DPG responses? This tests whether:

-   Dim nights: Multiple consecutive dim evenings produce cumulative effects on DPG
-   Bright nights: Multiple consecutive bright evenings produce cumulative effects on DPG

Key distinction from lag analysis: - Lag analysis: Tests whether Day\[t-1\], Day\[t-2\] each add independent effects - Persistence analysis: Tests whether being on the 1st vs. 2nd vs. 3rd+ consecutive day of the same condition matters

## Dataset Preparation

```{r dpg-persistence-prep}
participant_list_dpg <- c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P09", "P10")

# Light patterns for DPG 
light_patterns_dpg <- list(
  P01 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P02 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P03 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P04 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P05 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P06 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P07 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P09 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P10 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "B", "D", "D")
)

dpg_persistence <- map_dfr(participant_list_dpg, ~{
  df <- ibuttons %>% 
    filter(id == .x) %>%
    # Extract session number from session variable (e.g., "C01_01" -> 1)
    mutate(exp_session = as.integer(gsub("C0[1-4]_", "", session))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(DPG_intervention)) %>%
    # Aggregate by session: take mean DPG_intervention per session
    group_by(id, exp_session) %>%
    summarise(DPG_intervention = mean(DPG_intervention, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(participant_id = id)
  
  # Get light pattern
  pattern_vec <- light_patterns_dpg[[.x]]
  
  if (.x == "P10") {
    # For P10: create indices for sessions excluding position 5
    # P10 has 13 positions in total, but position 5 is excluded
    # Sessions are: 1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13
    valid_sessions <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13)
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = valid_sessions, 
      Light_Lag0 = pattern_vec
    )
  } else {
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = seq_along(pattern_vec), 
      Light_Lag0 = pattern_vec
    )
  }
  
  df %>% left_join(light_df, by = "exp_session")
})

# Add demographics 
dpg_persistence <- dpg_persistence %>%
  left_join(participant_demographics_dpg, by = "participant_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Light_Lag0)) %>%
  filter(!(participant_id == "P10" & exp_session == 5)) %>%
  filter(participant_id != "P07") %>%  # Exclude P07
  arrange(participant_id, exp_session) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    condition_change = Light_Lag0 != lag(Light_Lag0, default = first(Light_Lag0)),
    run_id = cumsum(condition_change),
    run_length = ave(run_id, run_id, FUN = seq_along),
    run_length_dim = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", run_length, NA),
    run_length_bright = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "B", run_length, NA),
    Light_Lag0_num = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", 0, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    run_category_dim = factor(case_when(
      run_length_dim == 1 ~ "First",
      run_length_dim == 2 ~ "Second",
      run_length_dim >= 3 ~ "Third"
    ), levels = c("First", "Second", "Third")),
    run_category_bright = factor(case_when(
      run_length_bright == 1 ~ "First",
      run_length_bright == 2 ~ "Second",
      run_length_bright >= 3 ~ "Third"
    ), levels = c("First", "Second", "Third"))
  ) %>%
  select(participant_id, exp_session, DPG_intervention, Light_Lag0, Light_Lag0_num,
         run_length, run_length_dim, run_length_bright, 
         run_category_dim, run_category_bright, sex, age, bmi)

# Verify dataset
cat("Total observations:", nrow(dpg_persistence), "\n")
cat("Participants:", paste(unique(dpg_persistence$participant_id), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("P10 sessions:", paste(sort(dpg_persistence$exp_session[dpg_persistence$participant_id == "P10"]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Model 1: Linear Persistence Models, Dim Evenings

```{r dpg-persistence-dim-linear}
# Dim Evenings (all sessions), linear
dpg_persistence_dim <- dpg_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_length_dim))

model_persistence_dim_numeric <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ run_length_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = dpg_persistence_dim,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_numeric)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_numeric <- confint(model_persistence_dim_numeric, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_numeric)

# Dim Evenings WITHOUT Session 1, linear
dpg_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- dpg_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_length_dim), exp_session > 1)

model_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ run_length_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = dpg_persistence_dim_no_s1,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_no_s1)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- confint(model_persistence_dim_no_s1, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_no_s1)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 4 Persistence, Linear, Dim: To test whether consecutive dim light evenings produce cumulative effects on the distal-proximal skin temperature gradient during the light intervention window, the linear relationship between run length (number of consecutive dim evenings) and DPG was examined. Two models were fitted, whilst the first model includes all observations, the second model excludes Session 1, as there is no controlled light exposure on the previous day, which might influence results.

Including Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find a linear effect of consecutive dim evenings for average skin temperature gradient (β=0.1282, SE=0.1947, p=0.515).

Excluding Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find a linear effect of consecutive dim evenings for average skin temperature gradient (0.2968, SE=0.1985, p=0.146). Despite the visual impression that the DPG gradient is less negative, particularly on the third day of dim light, this visual trend could not be confirmed in the statistical analysis.

The positive (non-significant) coefficients suggest that with increasing number of consecutive dim nights, the DPG graident becomes less negative. However, findings did not reach statistical significance.

# Model 2: Linear Persistence Models, Bright Evenings


Interpretation Exploratory 4 Persistence, Linear, Bright: To test whether consecutive bright light evenings produce cumulative effects on average skin temperature gradient during the light intervention window, the linear relationship between run length (number of consecutive dim evenings) and DPG was examined. As the first evening light exposure was dim for all participants, the analysis including and excluding session 1 are the same.

No statistically significant linear persistence effect was found for consecutive bright evenings (β=-0.0163, SE=0.1663, p=0.923).

# Model 3: Categorical Persistence Models, Dim Evenings

```{r dpg-persistence-dim-categorical}
# Dim Evenings (all sessions), categorical
dpg_persistence_dim <- dpg_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_category_dim))

model_persistence_dim_categorical <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ run_category_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = dpg_persistence_dim,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_categorical)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_categorical <- confint(model_persistence_dim_categorical, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_categorical)

# Dim Evenings WITHOUT Session 1, categorical 
dpg_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- dpg_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_category_dim), exp_session > 1)

model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1 <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ run_category_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = dpg_persistence_dim_no_s1,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1 <- confint(model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 4 Persistence, Categorical, Dim: In order to examine potential non-linear patterns of cumulative dim light exposure on mean distal-proximal skin temperature gradient, a model was fitted using the categories second (2nd day cumulative dim light exposure) and third (3rd day cumulative dim light exposure) compared to the first dim night (reference category) to predict mean DPG values during the light intervention window. As in the linear persistence analysis, two models (first with, second without first experimental session) were fitted.

Including Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find non-linear effects of consecutive dim evenings for DPG values: Second (β=-0.3801, SE=0.3246, p=0.249), Third (β=0.5141, SE=0.3954, p=0.202).

Excluding Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find statistically significant non-linear effects of consecutive dim evenings for DPG values, however the effect of the third bright light evening almost reached statistical significance level: Second (β=-0.1461, SE=0.32, p=0.6587), Third (β=0.7745, SE=0.3948, p=0.0594).

# Model 4: Categorical Persistence Models, Bright Evenings

```{r dpg-persistence-bright-categorical}

# Bright Evenings WITHOUT Session 1, categorical

model_persistence_bright_categorical_no_s1 <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ run_category_bright + (1 | participant_id),
  data = dpg_persistence_bright_no_s1,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_bright_categorical_no_s1)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_bright_categorical_no_s1 <- confint(model_persistence_bright_categorical_no_s1, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_bright_categorical_no_s1)
```

Interpretation: In order to examine potential non-linear patterns of cumulative bright light exposure on mean skin temperature gradient during light intervention period, a model was fitted using the categories second (2nd day cumulative bright light exposure) and third (3rd day cumulative bright light exposure) compared to the first bright night (reference category) to predict DPG values As the first evening light exposure was dim for all participants, the analysis including and excluding session 1 are the same.

No statistically significant effects of the second consecutive bright evening was found for the second (β=-0.31031, SE=0.33753, p=0.365), and the third consecutive bright evening did not yield statistical significance (β=0.04873, SE=0.33753, p=0.886).

# Exploratory Analysis: Climate Chamber Temperature

An exploratory model including the temperature data from the climate chamber during the intervention window will be used to identify a potential impact of the climate temperature on distal-proximal gradient values. Despite efforts to keep the chamber at a constant temperature throughout and across sessions, some deviations happened, hence this analysis examines the robustness of findings to the inclusion of the climate chamber data.

## Load Climate Data and Use UNIX Column (Correct Timestamps)

```{r climate-load}
# Load climate data
climate_lab <- read_excel("C:/Users/anton/OneDrive/AfterGlow/data/raw/group/climate/01_climate_20250831T100000.xlsx")

str(climate_lab)
```

```{r climate-convert-unix}
# Convert UNIX timestamp to MESZ (UTC+2 for Munich summer time)
climate_lab$unix_converted <- as_datetime(climate_lab$UNIX, tz = "Europe/Berlin")

head(climate_lab)
```

## Group 1 Data Extraction & Processing

```{r climate-group1}
# Filter data
group1_dates <- seq(as.Date("2025-06-16"), by = "day", length.out = 11)
climate_group1_all <- climate_lab %>%
  filter(
    as.Date(unix_converted) %in% group1_dates,
    hour(unix_converted) == 21 & minute(unix_converted) >= 30 |
    hour(unix_converted) == 22 |
    hour(unix_converted) == 23 & minute(unix_converted) == 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    unix_converted = floor_date(unix_converted, unit = "minute"),
    temp_felt = (tg + tdb) / 2
  )

# Check missing data
gaps <- climate_group1_all %>%
  arrange(unix_converted) %>%
  group_by(as.Date(unix_converted)) %>%
  mutate(time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(unix_converted, lag(unix_converted), units = "mins"))) %>%
  filter(time_diff > 1) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Total obs:", nrow(climate_group1_all), "| Gaps > 1 min:", nrow(gaps), "\n\n")
table(as.Date(climate_group1_all$unix_converted))

# Daily average
temp_felt_daily <- climate_group1_all %>%
  group_by(date_only = as.Date(unix_converted)) %>%
  summarise(temp_felt_mean = mean(temp_felt, na.rm = TRUE), n_obs = n())
print(temp_felt_daily)
```

## Add Climate Temperature to ibuttons_lmm Dataset

```{r climate-join-ibuttons}
# Remove temperature columns if they exist
ibuttons_lmm <- ibuttons_lmm %>%
  select(-contains("temp_felt_mean"), -contains("date_only"))

# Create temperature lookup
temp_lookup_dpg <- bind_rows(
  temp_felt_daily %>% mutate(group = 1, participants = list(c("P01", "P02", "P03"))),
  temp_felt_daily_group2 %>% mutate(group = 2, participants = list(c("P04", "P05"))),
  temp_felt_daily_group3 %>% mutate(group = 3, participants = list(c("P06", "P07", "P09"))),
  temp_felt_daily_group4 %>% mutate(group = 4, participants = list(c("P10")))
) %>%
  unnest(participants) %>%
  group_by(participants, group) %>%
  mutate(exp_session = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(participant_id = participants, exp_session, temp_felt_mean, date_only)

# Join temperature data
ibuttons_lmm <- ibuttons_lmm %>%
  left_join(temp_lookup_dpg, by = c("participant_id", "exp_session"))

# Check result
ibuttons_lmm %>% 
  filter(participant_id == "P02", exp_session == 3) %>%
  select(participant_id, exp_session, DPG_intervention, temp_felt_mean, date_only)
```

## Fit LMM with Temperature as Fixed Effect

```{r climate-models-dpg}
# Model 1 m_temp: Temperature as predictor
m_temp_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_temp_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_temp_dpg <- confint(m_temp_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_temp_dpg)

# Model 2: Session + Temperature
m_session_temp_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ exp_session + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_session_temp_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_session_temp_dpg <- confint(m_session_temp_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_session_temp_dpg)

# Model 3: Lag 0 + Temperature 
m_lag0_temp_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ Light_Lag0_num + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_lag0_temp_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_lag0_temp_dpg <- confint(m_lag0_temp_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_lag0_temp_dpg)

# Model 4: Lag 1 + Temperature 
m_lag1_temp_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ Light_Lag1_num + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_lag1_temp_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_lag1_temp_dpg <- confint(m_lag1_temp_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_lag1_temp_dpg)

# Model 5: Lag 2 + Temperature 
m_lag2_temp_dpg <- lmer(
  DPG_intervention ~ Light_Lag2_num + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = ibuttons_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_lag2_temp_dpg)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_lag2_temp_dpg <- confint(m_lag2_temp_dpg, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_lag2_temp_dpg)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 5 Climate Data: To examine potential effects of laboratory sensed temperature on DPG values, sensitivity analyses including climate chamber temperature as a covariate were conducted:

-   Model m_temp_dpg: A significant effect of the sensed temperature on DPG values was observed (β=0.6542, SE=0.2436, p=0.00933). Thereby an increase in sensed temperature by 1°C was associated with an increase in around 0.65°C in the distal-proximal skin temperature gradient (i.e., DPG became less negative, indicating greater distal vasodilation).

-   Model m_session_temp_dpg: A significant effect for both sensed temperature (β=0.72502, SE=0.23627, p=0.00322) as well as experimental session number (β=-0.08596, SE=0.04093, p=0.04010). Thus an increase in 1°C of sensed temperature was associated with approximately an increase in 0.73°C of DPG, whereas an increase in experimental session number was associated with a decrease in DPG by around -0.086°C (more negative gradient).

-   Model m_lag0_temp_dpg: When controlling for sensed temperature (β=0.70046, SE=0.28172, p=0.0156), no effect of current evening light exposure could be found on mean DPG values (β=-0.07833, SE=0.24723, p=0.7525).

-   Model m_lag1_temp_dpg: Similarly when controlling for sensed temperature (β=0.64546, SE=0.24525, p=0.01075), no statistically significant effect of pior evenings light exposure could be found on DPG values (β=-0.06276, SE=0.21452, p=0.77093).

-   Model m_lag2_temp_dpg: Similarly when controlling for sensed temperature (β=0.65086, SE=0.24471, p=0.00998), no statistically significant effect of the light exposure two days before could be found for mean DPG values (β=-0.03041, SE=0.21405, p=0.88755 ).

In summary, despite consistent significant effects of an increase of sensed temperature being associated with an increase in DPG values, no significant effects of light exposure history (Lag 0, Lag 1, Lag 2) could be found wen controlling for ambient temperature.

## Helper Functions

```{r dpg-summary-helpers}
# Helper functions to extract coefficients from LMM
get_coef_lmm <- function(model, coef_name) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients
  if (coef_name %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    return(coefs[coef_name, "Estimate"])
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

get_p_lmm <- function(model, coef_name) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients
  if (coef_name %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    return(coefs[coef_name, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}
```

## Final Model Summary: m0_dpg

```{r dpg-final-model-summary}
# Extract components from m0_dpg
m0_dpg_coef <- summary(m0_dpg)$coefficients

# Variance components
vc_final_dpg <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m0_dpg))

cat("**Final Model: m0_dpg (Baseline - Random Intercept Only)**\n\n")

cat("**Fixed Effects:**\n")
cat("Intercept:", round(m0_dpg_coef["(Intercept)", "Estimate"], 3), "°C\n")
cat("  SE:", round(m0_dpg_coef["(Intercept)", "Std. Error"], 3), "\n")
cat("  p:", format.pval(m0_dpg_coef["(Intercept)", "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 3, eps = 0.001), "\n\n")

cat("**Variance Components:**\n")
cat("Between-participant (Random Intercept):", round(vc_final_dpg$vcov[1], 3), "\n")
cat("Within-participant (Residual):", round(vc_final_dpg$vcov[2], 3), "\n\n")

# Calculate ICC
icc_final_dpg <- vc_final_dpg$vcov[1] / (vc_final_dpg$vcov[1] + vc_final_dpg$vcov[2])
cat("ICC (Intraclass Correlation):", round(icc_final_dpg, 3), 
    paste0("(", round(icc_final_dpg * 100, 1), "% of variance between participants)"), "\n\n")

cat("**Model Fit:**\n")
cat("AIC:", round(AIC(m0_dpg), 1), "| BIC:", round(BIC(m0_dpg), 1), "\n")
cat("N obs:", nrow(ibuttons_lmm), "| N participants:", 
    length(unique(ibuttons_lmm$participant_id)), "\n")
cat("Family: Gaussian (identity link)\n\n")
```

```{r}
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1,
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# --- Plot 4: Triplet 1.5h ---
p4 <- ggplot(df_plot_dpg_triplet_int_noP07, aes(x = triplet, y = mean_dpg_int)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = triplet), outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 42),
             size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7, shape = 16) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = triplet_colors) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = triplet_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min, y_max), breaks = y_breaks) +
  labs(
    title = "Triplets \u2013 1.5-h intervention",
    x = "Triplet",
    y = "Mean Distal-Proximal Gradient (\u00b0C)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1,
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# --- Combine ---
(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Distal-proximal skin temperature gradient under light exposure doublets and triplets",
    subtitle = "Mean DPG of the second / third day per sequence type (5-h exposure & 1.5-h intervention; P07 excluded)",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 24, hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 10))
    )
  )
```
